reuse.why: Follows the existing getCategoriesWithSavedTemplates pattern with a set-returning helper, but parses the tag with its own case-insensitive FIXED_TAG regex instead of the shared tag parser (extractTagsFromText in shared/tags.ts, which is case sensitive and handles '##' escaping).

duplication.why: The same 'fetch fixed set, then if fixed.has(id) skip' block is pasted into all six month-wide actions on top of their already-duplicated category-selection queries, instead of folding the exclusion into a single selection.

placement.why: The helper sits in budget/actions.ts next to the template-exclusion helper, where the month-wide selection logic lives.

scope.why: Only the six month-wide actions, a test and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: The tag rule has one definition, but the month-wide exclusion set is still assembled separately in every action (SQL filter, template set, fixed set, income check), so the next exclusion needs six more edits.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getCategoriesInFixedGroups (budget/actions.ts) matches '#fixed' with its own regex instead of using the tag extraction in shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated fixed.has checks are verbatim copies, not disguised.

one_place.where: getCategoriesInFixedGroups/FIXED_TAG in budget/actions.ts define the #fixed rule and every month-wide action calls it, though each applies the skip with its own check.
